quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

37 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects your stopping ability. Slow down when roads are poor or slippery. Driving too fast on bad roads puts you at risk if you need to stop suddenly.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing without flashing signals or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at railroad crossings, especially if there are no lights or gates. Do not cross until your entire vehicle fits on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle might stall.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for vehicles and pedestrians to clear before going.

questions.question: What do pentagon-shaped signs indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagon-shaped signs mark school zones. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, you may pass if:
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are difficult to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than larger vehicles.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are difficult to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers did not see motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians. These are harder to spot because they are smaller and may have less noticeable lights. Stay alert to protect these road users.

questions.question: If a green arrow turns into a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
May no longer turn and must go straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer have to turn in the direction the arrow showed.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you may still turn in the arrow's direction, but you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic first.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the right lane will end soon.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is reasonable and prudent.
A speed that is safe for existing conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drive at a reasonable and prudent speed for the area, traffic, weather, road condition, and light. Always stay within the legal speed limit and drive safely for current conditions.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has many turns and curves.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
Do not make any sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make any sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, avoid sudden speed or direction changes. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beams. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by the other vehicle's headlights. This lets you see the road and stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: You may have to attend a driver improvement clinic if you get ____ points against your license.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seven points
questions.explanation: If you get seven points against your license, you may have to attend a driver improvement clinic. Completing the clinic removes three points from your record.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped with yellow backgrounds and black markings. They alert drivers to unexpected road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when a car has bright headlights coming toward you?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road and away from the bright headlights. This keeps you from being blinded until the car passes.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection with a green light, but traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Take the right-of-way since you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: You can enter the intersection to prepare for your left turn if the light is green. Wait in the center until oncoming traffic passes, then complete your turn.

questions.question: You see a stopped school bus on the other side of a center turning lane on a three-lane road. What must you do?

options.text: Should honk their horn before passing the bus on its left.
May continue driving when they think most kids are done exiting the bus.
Must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop for a stopped school bus on the opposite side of a center turning lane. You can only move when the stop arm is raised and the lights stop flashing.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. If your brakes fail, your car will not roll into traffic.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Tell other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians your plans by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your horn when needed.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and look for pedestrians and other traffic.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and look for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and look for pedestrians and other traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely and look for pedestrians and other traffic. Wait until the intersection is clear before you go.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: A circular sign warns of a railroad crossing. This sign tells you that a train crossing is coming and you should watch for trains.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic go first before you enter the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downhill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that there is a steep hill ahead.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stopped on the opposite side of a center turning lane on a four-lane road, drivers:

options.text: Must stop until the school bus starts moving.
Must stop until the stop arm is raised.
Must stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: May continue driving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a center turning lane on a four-lane road, you may continue driving. However, always drive carefully near a stopped school bus.

questions.question: This sign warns that you are approaching:
questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, turn your steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the car to go. Once the car straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: When a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes loses grip on a slippery road, drivers should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: If your car loses grip on a slippery road with Anti-Lock Brakes, press hard on the brake pedal and hold it while steering away from danger. The system automatically pumps the brakes faster than you can. Releasing pressure or pumping the brakes will turn off the system.

questions.question: Your body removes approximately:
questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink per hour.
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one alcoholic drink per hour. However, many factors affect how impaired you become, including how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your body weight, how much you have eaten, and your general health.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels sharply toward the road edge. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead is low. Do not drive under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming hill.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you of a steep hill. Adjust your speed to drive safely.

questions.question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol help reduce impairment?

options.text: Yes, it decreases blood alcohol concentration.
Yes, it cancels the effect of the alcohol.
No, it has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
No, it increases blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober or change your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and yield for trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield for trains.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when you approach it. Trains cannot yield to cars, so you must wait for them to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: The traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: At a solid yellow light, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What does a solid white line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Lanes move in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Lanes move in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Lanes move in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Lanes move in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes move in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.
